description: completeReviewWithFindings, a method on the persistence adapter, orchestrates an entire multi-step business transaction (mark running, insert each finding, compute the verdict via business rules, set the verdict) instead of that orchestration living in the domain/application layer, which this codebase's real ReviewRepository port and ReviewOrchestrator otherwise cleanly separate.

required_findings.justification: This codebase's real ReviewRepository port is read-only (listRepositoriesForUser/listReviewsForUser/getReviewById) precisely because writes and business-rule orchestration belong to the domain/orchestrator layer, not the persistence adapter. Here, completeReviewWithFindings both sequences multiple writes AND computes the verdict policy (a P0 finding blocks approval) directly inside the adapter — transaction orchestration and business-rule evaluation have leaked into what should be a thin persistence boundary.

explanation: A concrete example of orchestration logic placed in the wrong layer: the whole multi-step sequence (three separate calls plus an inline verdict computation) is visible in one method. allowed_categories also accepts the business-logic-leakage framing, since the verdict computation embedded here is the same underlying issue as `responsibility-separation-01`'s, just in the persistence layer instead of the controller layer.
